rationale: The assistant correctly narrowed the fault to the rear-right zone's power side (element/limiter vs board relay), kept both possibilities open, asked for the full model and PNC before any part, and steered toward a Zanussi/appliance engineer, matching the ground truth direction. Weaknesses: the opening message bizarrely asked whether 'hob' meant software and referenced a working directory, and the final message offered multimeter testing for a 'competent DIYer' (isolated at the breaker, so not live work, but still beyond the expected no-dismantling boundary and offered without asking whether the customer had a meter or would remove the hob). It never probed the 'slow before failing' history that would have strengthened the element hypothesis, but overall a real homeowner would be reasonably well served.
